key_insight: The paper introduces two Lean 4 benchmarks that show current AI agents can complete quantum theorem proofs, but performance is still limited and improves meaningfully when a verified library is added.
engineering_relevance: These benchmarks provide a reproducible way to measure and compare proof-agent reliability for quantum algorithms and quantum information, helping guide development of practical AI-assisted formal verification tools.
method: Built Lean-QA-Bench (36 tasks) and Lean-QIT-Bench (40 tasks) for theorem completion in quantum computing.
Evaluated four models under two modes: task-only baseline and library-augmented deduction (LAD).
Used deterministic proof checking plus targeted semantic review, with difficulty weights assigned before model execution.
evidence_signal: Across eight model-benchmark comparisons, LAD improved both score and completion rate, with top difficulty-weighted scores reaching 60.4/100 on quantum algorithms and 59.6/100 on quantum information.
watch_item: Results depend on a fixed Lean environment and benchmark-specific verified libraries, so generalization to broader quantum theorem proving or different toolchains may be limited.
paper_title: Benchmarking Agents for Proving Theorems in Quantum Algorithms and Quantum Information
